22455:

  • An action protocol must be applied by schools when the CO2 standard is exceeded.

25793:
• This bill strengthens secularism in public and private schools in Québec.
  • It adds rules on uncovered faces, religious symbols, religious accommodations and the quality of teaching.
Part 1 Education Act
  • The public school system must respect democratic values, equality between men and women, and the secularism of the State.
  • Students must have their faces uncovered on school premises, in vocational training or in adult education.
  • Children schooled at home and their parents must also have their faces uncovered when receiving services from a school service centre.
  • Anyone providing services to students or in contact with them must have their face uncovered.
  • Students must respect equality between men and women and must not engage in bullying or violence related to racism, sexual orientation or disability.
  • Schools, vocational training centres and adult education centres must adopt codes of conduct that include these requirements.
  • The ban on wearing a religious symbol now extends to staff of school service centres and certain people under a service contract.
  • This ban does not apply to staff already employed or contracts already in effect when the law is passed.
  • Requests for leave on religious grounds by school employees are better regulated and may sometimes be refused, particularly regarding mandatory school attendance.
  • People who work with students, as well as members of governing boards and school service centres, must act without religious consideration.
  • School service centres must adopt a code of ethics for members of governing boards.
  • School and centre premises cannot be used for religious practices.
  • No one may use a religious belief to influence a decision under this Act.
  • Teachers must submit a teaching plan to their principal, who must evaluate it every year.
  • A new committee on the quality of educational services helps principals monitor this quality.
  • The minister may set the exam schedule and order a school service centre to comply with a law or government rule.
  • Certain decisions by the minister, such as suspending a teaching licence, apply even if the teacher challenges them before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • French-speaking staff and people working with students must communicate with them and with each other only in French.
Part 2 Act respecting private education
  • Staff members of a private school not recognized for subsidy purposes must also have their faces uncovered.
  • Private institutions must also adopt such codes of conduct.
Part 3 Education Act and Act respecting private education
  • Some rules apply even if they conflict with the Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms or the Constitution of 1982.
Part 4 Regulation respecting ethics standards for French-language school service centres
  • Technical adjustments to align with the new secularism rules.

• This bill brings in measures from the 25 March 2025 budget and amends 38 laws or regulations, mainly in tax, municipal, and vehicle matters.
  • Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan: work will only be considered done in Québec if it is also performed in Canada, for the purpose of calculating pensions.
  • Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan: the calculation of benefits will exclude months where a person receives a reduced CNESST benefit.
  • Highway Safety Code and Regulation respecting road vehicle registration: the value threshold for a vehicle that triggers an additional fee rises from $40,000 to $62,500.
  • Highway Safety Code: the exemption from this fee for electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles priced between $40,000 and $75,000 is removed.
  • Highway Safety Code: a new additional fee will apply to electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles for their registration or right to operate.
  • Act respecting the Institut de la statistique du Québec: clarifies the rules for when the Institute collects information for a public body.
  • Act respecting the Institut de la statistique du Québec: more researchers linked to a public body will be allowed to use information held by the Institute for research purposes.
  • Code of Civil Procedure: changes how the seizable portion of income is calculated for a person who owes child or spousal support.
  • Code of Civil Procedure: support payments granted to an adult child can no longer be seized.
  • Act to facilitate the payment of support: a person who receives last-resort financial assistance will no longer need to provide a guarantee for the collection of their support payments.
  • Act to facilitate the payment of support: in a state of emergency, the Minister of Finance will be able to adjust collection fees and advances paid to support-receiving parents.
  • Tax Administration Act: the calculation to determine whether a corporation is a "large corporation" will now include the capital of related corporations.
  • Tax Administration Act: tax information may be shared with the Minister of Finance without consent, to assess economic or budgetary policies.
  • Act respecting insurers: insurers will be able to obtain information on a deceased person from Revenu Québec and the Registrar of Civil Status, to inform life insurance beneficiaries of amounts owed to them.
  • Act respecting municipal taxation: municipalities will no longer be allowed to collect a business tax, except for certain assessments by business development corporations.
  • Act respecting municipal taxation: municipalities will no longer be allowed to establish a rental value roll for businesses.
  • Miscellaneous measures: more funding is provided for the Fonds Avenir Mécénat Culture.
  • Miscellaneous measures: the fee to consult the land register (which lists rights over properties) is revised.
  • Act to reduce the debt and establish the Generations Fund: the government's debt reduction targets for 2032-2033 and 2037-2038 are increased.
  • Act respecting parental insurance: the government will be able to change contribution rates for the parental insurance plan by government rule, without a new vote in the Assembly.

• This bill amends 117 laws and regulations to reorganize government structures, simplify processes and increase the accountability of senior officials.
  • It merges, abolishes or transforms several public bodies and transfers their duties elsewhere.
Part 1 Act respecting the National Institute of Excellence in Health and Social Services
  • Merges this institute and the National Institute of Public Health into one body, the Québec Institute of Health and Social Services.
Part 2 Act respecting health and social services governance
  • Urgences-santé's board of directors will be made up of the same members as Santé Québec's board.
  • Santé Québec will provide administrative services to Urgences-santé.
Part 3 Act respecting Héma-Québec and the Biovigilance Committee
  • Héma-Québec will take over coordination of organ donation, removed from Transplant Québec.
Part 4 Act respecting the Commission d'évaluation de l'enseignement collégial
  • This commission, which evaluated CEGEPs, is abolished.
Part 5 Act establishing the Office Québec-Monde pour la jeunesse
  • This body is folded directly into the Ministry of International Relations and La Francophonie.
Part 6 Act respecting the Office franco-québécois pour la jeunesse
  • Its internal organization is revised.
Part 7 Act respecting the Centre de la francophonie des Amériques
  • This centre becomes a non-profit organization instead of a public body.
Part 8 Charter of the French Language
  • The Minister of the French Language gains new responsibilities regarding Canadian Francophonie.
Part 9 Act respecting parental insurance
  • The Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale is abolished; Retraite Québec will now manage this plan and its fund.
Part 10 Act respecting the Ministère des Finances
  • The minister will have to present a comprehensive financial plan to fight climate change in the budget.
  • The government will be able to decide, by a government rule without a new vote, how to divide surpluses from the Electrification and Climate Change Fund between the Generations Fund and the Land Transportation Fund.
Part 11 Act respecting the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale
  • Its Information Technology Fund is abolished, its assets and debts transferred to the government's general fund.
  • A university fund, the Fonds 3 pour l'excellence et la performance universitaires, is also abolished and transferred to the general fund.
  • Two community assistance funds, the Fonds d'aide à l'action communautaire autonome and the Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales, are merged into one.
Part 12 Public Service Act
  • The Commission de la fonction publique is abolished; its tasks move to the Administrative Labour Tribunal.
Part 13 Act respecting administrative justice
  • The Administrative Tribunal of Québec will provide administrative services to the Financial Markets Administrative Tribunal.
Part 14 Act respecting the marketing of agricultural, food and fish products
  • Reduces the number of vice-chairs and members needed to decide certain matters at the Régie des marchés agricoles.
Part 15 Act respecting the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec
  • The government will now appoint the SAAQ's vice-presidents and set their salaries.
Part 16 Act respecting the governance of state-owned enterprises
  • The management of the CEOs of Hydro-Québec, the Commission de la construction du Québec and other state-owned enterprises will have to be reviewed by a parliamentary committee at least every 4 years.
Part 17 Public Administration Act
  • Specifies that every senior official must act with prudence, efficiency and fairness in their duties.
  • A new 2-year probationary period will apply to anyone appointed as a state administrator.
  • During this probationary period, the government will be able to dismiss a state administrator who was not already a permanent public servant, with simple written notice of 15 days.
Part 18 Act respecting contracting by public bodies
  • Removes the requirement to periodically renew authorizations to contract with the government.
Part 19 Act respecting the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales
  • Its contracts and those carried out for certain groupings will be subject to the same rules as government enterprises.
Part 20 Act respecting the Société d'habitation du Québec
  • Allows housing bureaus to be merged and new ones created for any territory designated by the government.
  • Ends joint management of contributions paid by organizations receiving housing financial assistance.
Part 21 Several financial sector laws (including the Securities Act and the Act respecting the regulation of the financial sector)
  • Reduce the frequency of certain reports and remove the requirement to produce certain documents.
Part 22 Act respecting the regulation of the financial sector
  • The Autorité des marchés financiers, which oversees financial institutions, will have to make certain data and analyses available online.
Part 23 Sustainable Development Act, Act respecting sustainable forest development and Pay Equity Act
  • Contain technical adjustments related to the sustainable development strategy, the chief forester and pay equity.

• Québec would be divided into 80 ridings and 17 electoral regions, for a total of 129 seats in the National Assembly.
  • Each voter would have two votes: one for a riding candidate, one for a candidate or list in their region.

  • 49 regional seats would be shared out based on votes won across the region, with an adjustment to balance results between parties.
  • A party must get at least 4% of the votes in Québec to be entitled to regional seats.
  • Parties would have to present as many women as men on their regional lists, alternating between them.
  • For riding candidates, parties would have to present between 40% and 60% women.
  • Rules are set out to replace a member if a regional seat becomes vacant.
  • Party and candidate financing rules would be adjusted to account for the two types of seats.
  • Election spending limits would be changed, while keeping roughly the same overall cap as before.

26993:
• This bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders (such as the Order of Nurses or the Order of Pharmacists).
  • It also allows certain health professionals to do more than before, without waiting for a doctor.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without the approval of the Office des professions or the Québec Cabinet.
  • The Office des professions, which oversees professional orders, will now approve certain regulations instead of the Québec Cabinet.
  • The Office des professions will alone decide which diplomas give access to a permit, through a regulation approved by the Québec Cabinet.
  • The Office des professions will have to create a common rule to settle disagreements over bills between a professional and their client.
  • The Office des professions will be able to impose common rules on several professional orders at once.
  • The Office des professions will alone decide the ethics rules for members of the boards of directors of the orders, and will be able to investigate and sanction them.
  • Orders will have to include more information in their public list of members (the roll).
  • The number of signatures needed to request a special general meeting of an order is changing.
  • People holding a psychotherapist permit obtained elsewhere in Canada will be able to practise in Québec, under new rules.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to start examinations and tests in more situations than before.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, medications, other substances, products and dressings, according to upcoming rules.
  • The rule limiting voting rights at meetings to section delegates only is removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide contraception more often.
  • They will also be able to screen more broadly for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections.
  • They will be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms if their test is positive.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Optometrists will have fewer limits on the medications they can prescribe or provide, and on the care they offer.
Part 5 Dietitians-nutritionists
  • Their field of practice is updated, and they will no longer need a medical prescription for certain reserved activities.
Part 6 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on Psychotherapy will cease operations.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • Students will be able to carry out certain psychotherapist activities during their training, if authorized by the Office des professions.
Part 7 Agronomists Act
  • Whether an activity is paid or not will no longer determine whether it counts as practising the profession of agronomist.
Part 8 Pharmacy Act
  • The Québec Cabinet will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or substitute a medication with another made by a company in which they have an interest, under conditions.
Part 9 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A drug manufacturer will be able to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a pharmacy banner or chain.
Part 10 Regulation respecting manufacturers and wholesalers
  • Manufacturers will also be able to pay these benefits to drug wholesalers, not only pharmacies.
  • Several other acts (Bar, notaries, land surveyors, denturology, medical imaging technologists, legal aid, Charter of the French language) receive related coordinating changes linked to these amendments.

• This bill sets out rules for exploring and operating underground reservoirs and certain fluids in Québec, mainly by amending the Act respecting underground gas storage and gas and oil pipelines.

  • The Minister of Labour now decides on changes to a decree requested by a joint committee or a contracting party.
  • The minister may approve, amend or cancel the by-laws of joint committees (bodies that oversee the application of decrees).

  • The minister no longer has to publish in newspapers a notice of requests to extend or amend a decree.

  • Imposes a requirement for an advisory opinion from the Court of Appeal on the legality of the proposed override

  • The Committee advises the government, monitors the development of the right, and publishes a report at least every 3 years.
  • The government must assess the impact of its decisions on the right to food and mitigate any negative effects.
  • Aims in particular at access to adequate food at school and the reduction of food waste.
  • Amends the Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms to include this new right to food.

  • Creates a national strategy for the autonomy and home support of older persons.

  • Provides for tax measures, rent regulation and support for caregivers.
